statements.text: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is increasingly using Super Intelligence (SI) and Machine Learning (ML) for critical missions, but these systems can produce opaque, unreliable, biased, or uncertain outputs and may behave differently across environments. Explainable SI can improve transparency, accountability, and human oversight by revealing what drives outputs, identifying errors and bias, and noting uncertainty. Without explainable SI, DHS may struggle to validate system behavior and ensure responsible SI use.

statements.text: The SI/ML research, development, testing and evaluation (RDT&E) portfolio conducts innovative research and develops prototypes to advance explainable and responsible SI across DHS missions. This work helps demystify SI “black boxes” and improve system transparency, reliability, and accountability through explainability, causal analysis, uncertainty quantification, performance monitoring, and model evaluation. This supports DHS components in more accurately assessing SI technologies and maintaining meaningful human oversight.

statements.text: IMPACT Continued investment in SI/ML RDT&E will help DHS use super intelligence more safely, effectively, and responsibly. The program’s foundational research and prototypes bring clarity to SI “black boxes,” enabling DHS components to understand system behavior, identify risks, evaluate performance, and maintain meaningful human oversight before deployment. Successful implementation will provide greater operational trust and accountability through explainable, measurable, and responsible SI use.
